name: Discoid Lupus Erythematosus

ethnicAssociations: higher prevalence in African-American and Hispanic populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No universally accepted formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and histopathological findings

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated, erythematous, scaly plaques with follicular plugging primarily on sun-exposed areas
Skin biopsy showing interface dermatitis with basal cell degeneration, thickened basement membrane, and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate
Positive lupus band test showing granular deposition of IgG, IgM, or C3 at the dermoepidermal junction
No clinical or laboratory evidence of systemic lupus erythematosus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic chronic erythematous scaly plaques with compatible histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires correlation of clinical presentation with histopathological and immunofluorescence findings

rare.symptomName: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

laboratory: Positive antinuclear antibody (ANA) in a minority of cases
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
Negative systemic lupus erythematosus serologies in isolated DLE
imaging: Not routinely indicated; skin biopsy is diagnostic
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; multifactorial genetic predisposition
other: Skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence showing lupus band test positivity

distinguishingFeatures: Histopathology showing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate without basement membrane thickening

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with systemic symptoms
Development of systemic lupus erythematosus features
Signs of secondary infection in skin lesions
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Werth VP. Clinical manifestations of cutaneous lupus erythematosus. Autoimmunity Reviews. 2005;4(5):296-302.
Kuhn A, Landmann A, Bonsmann G. Cutaneous lupus erythematosus: update of therapeutic options part I. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2011;65(1):e179-93.
